description: Heat flooding housing infrastructure and public health remain fragmented across governance systems.
Deferred maintenance and fragmented finance create long-term service fragility.
Food water land and biodiversity systems are governed through fragmented institutions despite strong interdependence.
Public trust is weakened by accountability gaps service failures exclusion and legitimacy deficits.
Care systems rely on hidden labor buffers and underfunded workforce capacity.
AI deployment risks outpacing procurement rights appeals and oversight capacity.
Energy transition pressure interacts with grid resilience affordability permitting and public legitimacy.
Learning systems struggle to build civic ecological technical and anticipatory capacity for uncertain futures.
